findings.desc: scope_extension_proposal does not persist the proposal body when a separate reason is supplied. The CLI schema asks for proposal plus optional reason, and ScopeExtensionProposal has proposal/proposalTextHash fields for the human-readable expansion proposal, but the handler calls buildScopeExtensionProposal with only reason: args.reason || args.proposal and patch: {}, so args.proposal is discarded whenever reason is present (packages/main/src/handlers/scope-anti-expansion.ts:246). The builder used by the handler never writes proposal/proposalTextHash (packages/main/src/core/scope-anti-expansion.ts:656), while the typed artifact builder below does preserve them (packages/main/src/core/scope-anti-expansion.ts:960). This means the gate-consumed scope-extension-proposals.json can block INIT_CHECK but not reliably record what expansion was proposed, undermining the proposal/discard/decision audit flow required for INIT reviewers to propose rather than mutate scope.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 07ceb003: scope_extension_proposal now passes args.proposal into buildScopeExtensionProposal; proposal/proposalTextHash persist separately from reason. Verified by npm --prefix packages/main run test:scope-anti-expansion-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run build, and node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs.

findings.desc: The INIT scope anti-expansion gate can be satisfied with empty boundary artifacts. Evidence: cli-engine.ts:501-520 declares scope_boundary_set.allowedScope as an array without min(1), and execution_boundary_set has all boundary fields optional. handlers/scope-anti-expansion.ts:183-215 writes scope/execution artifacts without requiring any allowed/excluded scope term or command/tool policy; this differs from story-create.ts:466-472, which does require a non-empty initial allowed scope. core/scope-anti-expansion.ts:532-616 evaluates existing empty artifacts as a pass when no keyword/repeat issues exist, and machine.ts:189-225 then only checks stored pass/hash/freshness. A caller can save empty scope/execution boundaries, run scope_freeze_check, and satisfy the scope gate with no effective user-confirmed boundary.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 07ceb003: scope boundary builder/CLI require non-empty allowed scope and execution boundary builder/CLI require at least one command/tool/path allow/block entry. Verified by scope anti-expansion smoke empty-boundary cases, build, and process fact contract.

findings.desc: story_create can create INIT_CHECK stories that cannot satisfy or repair the new scope gate. Evidence: the fromDraft branch writes the new story directly with phase INIT_CHECK and deletes the draft without writing scope-boundary.json, execution-boundary.json, or scope-freeze-check.json (handlers/story-create.ts:247-351). The CLI then calls dev_start directly for that result (cli-engine.ts:3819-3829). dev_start now rejects INIT_CHECK/no-worktree stories when getScopeAntiExpansionGuardFailureReason reports missing scope artifacts (handlers/worktree.ts:632-638). The only commands that can create or refresh those artifacts are INIT-only by handler and policy (handlers/scope-anti-expansion.ts:74-79; core/command-policy.ts:287-291), so fromDraft leaves the story stuck in INIT_CHECK with no normal CLI repair path. The direct story_create phase=INIT_CHECK path has the same shape: it can write scope/execution artifacts but never writes a freeze check, and scope_freeze_check is no longer callable after phase INIT_CHECK.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 07ceb003: story_create refuses direct phase=INIT_CHECK and fromDraft now materializes at INIT so normal init-check and scope gates can run before worktree creation. Verified by direct INIT_CHECK smoke, build, and contract.

findings.desc: execution_boundary_set path-boundary support is inconsistent across CLI, handler, core, and policy. Evidence: cli-engine.ts:510-520 exposes allowedPaths/blockedPaths; core/scope-anti-expansion.ts:293-310 builds and hashes allowedPaths/excludedPaths with safe relative path validation; types.ts defines ExecutionBoundaryData path fields; command-policy.ts:288 says the execution boundary covers commands and paths. But handlers/scope-anti-expansion.ts:88-96 rejects any allowedPaths/blockedPaths and claims core ExecutionBoundaryData only defines command/tool fields. This makes the documented CLI surface unusable and leaves registry/policy claims out of sync with runtime behavior.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 07ceb003: execution_boundary_set accepts allowedPaths/blockedPaths/excludedPaths and delegates safe relative path validation to core. Verified by handler safe-path smoke and build.

findings.desc: Docs/prompt say the INIT reviewer must route scope expansion through scope_extension_proposal and must not mutate checklist/scope boundary (docs/requirements/decisions/story-lifecycle.md:86; packages/main/templates/agents/koala-review-story-init.md:513), but the mechanical contract still exposes a direct checklist mutation path in INIT: DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS includes checklist_update in INIT (packages/main/src/core/config.ts:184-190), COMMAND_POLICIES allows checklist_update in INIT as storyScopedMutating (packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts:147), and checklist_update can change title/context/excludes while story.phase is INIT because title/context are protected only from INIT_CHECK onward and the handler writes item.title/item.context/item.excludes (packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:331,373,377,388-390). scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs inventories scope_extension_proposal/decide and checklist_update separately but does not assert the INIT-reviewer-only-proposal invariant (scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs:118-119,3154-3187). This leaves the anti-expansion rule prompt-only rather than prompt + CLI/contract protected, so a reviewer or misrouted INIT actor can widen checklist scope without producing a pending proposal/explicit decision trail.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 07ceb003: INIT reviewer lanes koala-review-story-init/product-reviewer are mechanically blocked from checklist_add or checklist_update definition mutations in INIT and must use scope_extension_proposal; process fact contract now asserts this invariant. Verified by INIT reviewer mutation smoke and contract verifier.

findings.desc: fromDraft coverage is stale/conflicting after the F-003 fix. The implementation now materializes fromDraft stories in INIT (packages/main/src/handlers/story-create.ts:330,354), and the CLI auto-dev_start branch only triggers for legacy output containing `(phase=INIT_CHECK)` (packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:3844). The new scope anti-expansion smoke covers direct phase=INIT_CHECK rejection (packages/main/src/tasks/scope-anti-expansion-smoke.ts:303-317), and the contract verifier only checks for the fromDraft output string `(INIT)` (scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs:3170-3177); it does not run a fromDraft behavior smoke for the new INIT semantics. Meanwhile the existing fromDraft behavioral smoke still asserts the old behavior: story.phase === INIT_CHECK, worktree metadata exists, and output mentions worktree/main merge (packages/main/src/tasks/worktree-authority-smoke.ts:300-307,365-371). Repro: `npm --prefix packages/main run test:worktree-authority-smoke` fails with actual `INIT` vs expected `INIT_CHECK` at dist/tasks/worktree-authority-smoke.js:287. Therefore smoke/contract coverage does not cleanly cover the updated direct INIT_CHECK/fromDraft behavior, and the repository retains a stale failing smoke around the exact reviewed finding.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 2a355f947: worktree-authority-smoke now expects fromDraft stories to stop at INIT, commits bounded from-draft metadata on main, and verifies explicit story_advance INIT_CHECK performs the worktree bootstrap. Verified by npm --prefix packages/main run test:worktree-authority-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run test:scope-anti-expansion-smoke, npm --prefix packages/main run build, and node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs.

findings.desc: Scope discard digest protection is only exercised when a prior digest is preloaded into the same current story, but the real discard path writes scope-discard-digest.json back to the story being discarded and the INIT_CHECK gate reads only store.readScopeDiscardDigest(currentStoryId). A newly created replacement story therefore starts with an empty digest and can repeat a discarded direction without mitigation, contrary to CHK-004/user-visible repeat-discard protection. Source: packages/main/src/handlers/worktree.ts:568-599 writes the digest under the discarded storyId; packages/main/src/core/machine.ts:163-173 consumes only the current storyId digest; packages/main/src/tasks/scope-anti-expansion-smoke.ts:469-478 seeds the previous digest into the same story instead of driving the real discard→new-story flow.
